title: Standalone components, and the NgModule code you will still meet

videos.script:
Every Angular file you write from now on is a component, or something a component uses. {{anatomy}} Today you read one field by field. The selector is its tag. The template is what it draws. And the imports list is what that template may use besides plain HTML.

{{error}} You will break that list on purpose. The build refuses with an error called NG8001, and you learn to read it, because you will meet it again at work.

Then the code you will meet at work. {{module}} Until recently, every component belonged to a module, and the module decided what its template could use. You build a small project the old way, and read its module. {{migrate}} Then Angular's own migration converts it to standalone, in three steps, and you read what each step changed. The last step leaves a wrapper behind, and the lesson explains why it is there.

{{planner}} By the end, the planner has three components nested inside each other. The page does not show where one ends and the next begins. That is how it should be.
